rules.text: Before proposing a fix that deletes or replaces an rz(angle), check the resulting unitary matches the original to within allowance (eps_synth/N_Rz), not just approximately. A distance of ~0.2 vs required ~6e-5 means the replacement gate/angle is wrong, not just imprecise synthesis. Recompute the exact matrix product by hand or re-derive the angle algebraically before submitting.

When collapsing or merging rotations (e.g. fix op replacing gate at index 11 with identity/op0), verify the merged angle equals the sum/difference of the original rotation angles exactly (mod 2pi), including sign flips from any intervening h/s/x/z conjugations on that qubit.

A 'fix' proposal that removes a single rz without compensating for the Clifford gates around it on the same qubit will fail the operator-norm verifier; track the full Pauli-frame/basis change across the window before deleting or merging any rotation gate.

When a fix removes one rz on a qubit (e.g. op N->0), check whether OTHER rz gates on that same qubit later in the window need their angles updated too (not just the one adjacent to the deletion) -- the accepted q3/q1/q0 example changed three separate downstream rz angles, including sign flips, to compensate for deleting a single rz at index 25.

Before submitting fix op N->0 for a lone rz with no other rotation on that qubit in the window, compute the full window unitary with and without that gate; if they differ by more than eps_synth/N_Rz, the fix is invalid outright (not a candidate for later angle patching) -- do not propose bare deletions without first checking for compensating rz gates elsewhere on the same qubit.

After a fix op N->0 deletes an rz on qubit q, some later rz gates on q may need NO change if an intervening h or cx pair restores the frame to its pre-deletion state before that gate executes -- check frame parity at each candidate site rather than patching every rz on q uniformly.

Before submitting fix op N->0 for an rz with no other rz on that same physical qubit index, still check rz gates reached via cx-swaps of the logical qubit (q may be relabeled across cx q_a q_b boundaries); only skip angle-patching if truly no rz anywhere in the window shares that logical path, and verify via full window unitary diff against eps_synth/N_Rz.

When a fix removes one rz on qubit q (e.g. op N->0), check rz gates on OTHER qubits too, not just q: cx q_a q_b propagates the frame change across both qubits. The accepted q3/q1/q0 example patched angles on three different qubits (q3, q1, q0), not just q's own downstream rz chain.

A bare cx q_a q_b / cx q_a q_b pair is only identity if nothing acts between them; if your fix op leaves such a pair adjacent after deleting/moving gates, double check no rz/t/tdg on q_a or q_b was intended between them -- 'cx q1 q0 / cx q1 q0' with no payload is a near-certain verifier rejection, not a no-op.

Before submitting fix op N->0, simulate the full window unitary before and after the deletion yourself (not just angle bookkeeping); if the raw diff already exceeds eps_synth/N_Rz with no patch applied, do not submit the bare deletion as a candidate op -- compute the required patch first, then verify the patched version.

A fix proposal need not touch any rz: a pure Clifford window (only h/s/sdg/x/z/cx/cz) can still fail the operator-norm check if the proposed cx/h rewiring changes the overall permutation or basis mapping. Before submitting, simulate the full window (all Cliffords included) on basis inputs and diff against the original, not just the rz-bearing subcircuit.

When rewriting a block of cx gates among 3+ qubits (e.g. cx q2 q1 / cx q1 q2 / cx q2 q1 style swaps), check that your rewrite reproduces the exact qubit permutation of the original on ALL qubits in the window, including ones with only a single h or no gate -- dropping or reordering one cx changes which logical qubit later gates act on.

A bare cx q_a q_b / cx q_a q_b pair, or any even-length cx chain among the same qubits, is only identity if nothing acts between them AND the net permutation matches; before accepting such a pair as removable, verify via full window unitary diff -- 'cx q1 q0 / cx q1 q0' with no payload is a near-certain verifier rejection, not a no-op.

Zeroing an rz (op N->0) is only valid if that rotation's net effect is already identity under the surrounding Pauli frame -- it is not a safe default simplification. The rejection 'fix op 37->0: distance 1.893e-02' shows a nonzero rz was dropped without verifying it was conjugate to the identity; always full-window simulate before proposing op->0.

When simplifying rz(theta), first reduce theta into (-pi,pi] (or equivalent +/-2*pi*k form) rather than zeroing it: in the accepted fix, rz(8.7588...)->rz(2.4756...) and rz(9.7918...)->rz(-2.7744...) are mod-2pi reexpressions of the SAME angle, not deletions. Only propose op->0 if the reduced angle itself is ~0 after this step.

A near-miss rejection like 'op 24->0: distance 2.330e-04' (just above allowance 6.250e-05) often means the rotation is nearly but not exactly conjugate to identity -- do not round small residual angles to exactly 0; keep the residual rz or fold it into the adjacent Clifford's exact phase instead of truncating.

Before proposing op N->0 on an rz, confirm algebraically that the surrounding H/S/X/Z/CX sequence maps that rotation axis to itself with no net Pauli sign flip; if any conjugating gate maps Z-axis to X/Y axis, the rotation is NOT removable and must instead be re-expressed (angle change), not deleted.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 22: 0/2 with, 1/2 without across 13 shows -- not outperforming baseline; axis-mapping claim unsupported by acceptance data.)

rules.text: Repeated 'cx qA q3 / sdg q3 / h q3 / rz(theta) q3 / h q3 / s q3' blocks on q3 do NOT all conjugate rz the same way: the net Pauli frame on q3 accumulates across repetitions. Check each block's frame independently -- an rz removable in block 2 may not be removable in block 1 or 3 of the same chain.

When zeroing an rz inside an sdg/h/.../h/s wrapper, also check the immediately preceding rz on the same qubit: a valid fix may require renegating it (theta -> -theta) rather than leaving it unchanged, e.g. rz(3.292...)->rz(-2.991...) alongside a neighboring op->0, because the frame flip from the deleted gate propagates backward too.

High proposal-decline rate suggests: before proposing any op->0 in a chain of near-identical cx/sdg/h/rz/h/s blocks, compute the cumulative Clifford conjugation qubit-by-qubit from the start of the window, not block-locally -- an identical-looking block later in the chain can have a different effective frame than an earlier one.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 22: 0/0 with, 0/1 without -- no supporting evidence after many shows; redundant with R3/R18 cumulative-frame guidance.)

rules.text: Do not pattern-match 'zero the leading rz(q2)/rz(q1)/rz(q0) gates before the cx-chain' from past accepted fixes: those angles must individually be near 0 mod 2*pi already. Check each leading rz's reduced angle numerically before proposing op->0; zeroing non-small leading rotations causes large verifier distance (e.g. 6.136e-03).

A 't q_b' ... 'tdg q_b' pair that sandwiches a 'cx q_a q_b' in between is NOT a cancelling pair even though t/tdg are inverses: cx changes the effective operator the second gate conjugates. Example rejected at distance 3.902e-01: cx q0 q1 / t q1 / cx q0 q1 / tdg q1. Only remove t/tdg gates separated by cx after full window unitary diff, not just gate-list symmetry.

Before proposing op->0 on a leading rz(q_k) preceding a cx-chain, numerically compute the angle mod 2*pi yourself; do not infer zero-ability from a nearby accepted fix on a different qubit/angle. Rejected example: 'fix op 1->0, op 3->0: distance 6.136e-03' -- both angles were not actually near 0 mod 2*pi.

When reducing a chain of rz(theta) on the same qubit separated by cx/sdg/h/s wrappers, it is valid to reduce only some angles mod 2*pi and leave others unreduced (e.g. accepted fix kept rz(-2.9910505386396844) and rz(2.0877978489390117) unsimplified) -- partial-window fixes that zero only clearly-near-zero angles can still pass; do not force every rz in the block to resolve.

Rejected twice verbatim: 'fix op 3->0, op 7->0, op 11->0' (distance 5.369e-03). Proposing to zero MULTIPLE rz ops in one fix compounds error -- each must independently satisfy |angle mod 2*pi| ~ 0 well under the allowance; a batch of 3 near-small-but-nonzero angles sums to a distance far above allowance even if each alone might pass.

Before submitting a multi-op zeroing fix (op A->0, op B->0, op C->0 together), compute each angle's distance contribution separately first; if any single angle's reduced magnitude exceeds roughly the allowance, drop that op from the batch rather than submitting all three and failing on their combined distance.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 32: Duplicate of R25/R27 (same exact rejection 'op 3->0, op 7->0, op 11->0: distance 5.369e-03'); consolidating into R27 to stop diluting shown-count across three n)

rules.text: Before proposing op->0 on any rz (leading or not), numerically compute angle mod 2*pi yourself -- never infer zero-ability from a nearby accepted fix on a different qubit/angle, and never bundle several such zeroings into one fix without checking each individually: repeated rejection 'op 3->0, op 7->0, op 11->0: distance 5.369e-03' came from batching unverified angles.

A 'cx qA qB / rz(theta) qB / cx qA qB' block is only a no-op/simplifiable when qA is a known computational-basis state; it is NOT generally reducible to 'rz(theta) qB' or removable by symmetry alone. Rejected: cx q0 q1 / rz(0.04908...) q1 / cx q0 q1, distance 2.454e-02 even for small theta. Compute the controlled-rotation's full 4x4 action before proposing any such block as a fix.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Two rz with the SAME Pauli frame P (shown per rotation in the prompt) merge into one rz with the summed angle when every gate between them preserves P; the merge is exact (charge 0). Scan the window for equal-P pairs FIRST - this is the highest-value rewrite known.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] A gate between two rz preserves the rotation's frame iff it commutes with that Pauli: cx commutes with Z on its CONTROL (not its target), cz and rz commute with any Z-frame, h maps Z<->X. Check the path gate-by-gate before claiming a merge.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] If two equal-P rotations straddle sub-regions, prefer a fix block that sets ONE of them to 0 and lets the refit re-absorb the angle into the partner, instead of rewriting both regions by hand.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Snap rz(theta) to the nearest pi/4 multiple ONLY if 2|sin(delta/4)| <= allowance AND the saved gridsynth word (roughly 10-60 T at current eps_rz, shown in the prompt) exceeds any T added by the refit. A snap that fails either test will be rejected by the metric or the verifier.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Adjacent same-qubit pi/4 diagonals fold exactly: t;t = s, tdg;tdg = sdg, t;tdg = identity, s;s = z. Fold them whenever they appear - exact, free, and reduces explicit T count.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Never propose rz -> 0 unless 2|sin(theta/4)| <= allowance for THAT rotation, or the rest of the window is refit to compensate; zeroing a non-tiny rotation without compensation always fails the whole-window check.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Candidates may differ from the original by a GLOBAL phase only; a relative phase between basis branches is a real error the verifier measures. If a rewrite introduces s/z/t fix-ups, place them so branch phases match, not just the first column.

[seed 2026-10-18 FTQC primer] Change ONE thing per candidate (one merge, one snap, or one fold) and keep the rest of the window byte-identical; multi-edit candidates are rejected far more often and teach nothing when they fail.

[seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] Rotations are pi/4-parity-phase gadgets: two rz merge whenever their PARITIES agree, not only when they sit on the same qubit - re-routing a CNOT can make two rotations' parities equal, then they fuse to one rz(a+b). Look for a window rewrite that equalizes two rotation parities at the cost of Clifford-only changes.
rules.note: provenance: de Beaudrap, Bian, Wang, 'Fast and effective techniques for T-count reduction via spider nest identities', TQC 2020

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] In a Hadamard-free stretch the T-count is the number of DISTINCT odd parities in the phase polynomial. A candidate that reduces distinct odd parities beats one that only cancels adjacent gates; two equal odd parities kill 2 T at once.
rules.note: provenance: Heyfron & Campbell 'An efficient quantum compiler that reduces T count' (TODD, 2018); Vandaele, 'Lower T-count with faster algorithms', arXiv:2407.08695
